holidays.name: World Emoji Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of those tiny yellow faces and symbols we all use to say what words can't. People mark the day by flooding social media with their favorite emojis and sometimes throwing emoji-themed parties.
holidays.origin: Created in 2014 by Jeremy Burge of Emojipedia. The date, July 17, was chosen because it appears on the 📅 calendar emoji in Apple's design, which shows July 17.
holidays.funFact: The calendar emoji on iPhones displays July 17, and that is the reason the date was picked for World Emoji Day. Apple's choice dates back to the original Mac-era keynote announcement of iCal.

holidays.name: National Peach Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: A day for scooping up creamy, fruity peach ice cream at the peak of summer peach season. Fans make homemade batches with fresh, juicy peaches or grab a cone from the local creamery.
holidays.origin: The day is a food observance that falls in the middle of National Ice Cream Month, which was declared in July by President Ronald Reagan in 1984. Peach ice cream gets its own day as a summer favorite when peaches are at their ripest.
holidays.funFact: Peach ice cream was a favorite of early American ice cream makers, and it was often one of the first fruit flavors made at home with hand-cranked freezers.

holidays.name: National Yellow Pig Day
holidays.description: A delightfully absurd celebration of the number 17 through the mythical yellow pig. Mathematicians and fans gather to celebrate, sometimes with yellow-pig songs, stories, and pig-shaped snacks.
holidays.origin: It began in 1982 when two Princeton math students, Michael Spivak and Jeremy Cohen, were fascinated by the number 17 and a yellow pig. It spread through math departments, and the day falls on 7/17 because 17 is the sacred number of the yellow pig.
holidays.funFact: Yellow Pig Day has become a tradition at Harvey Mudd College and other colleges, where it has included singing yellow pig carols and even delivering yellow-pig-themed lectures about the number 17.

holidays.name: World Day for International Justice
holidays.description: A serious yet noteworthy observance that commemorates the adoption of the Rome Statute, which established the International Criminal Court. It highlights the global fight against impunity for the gravest crimes.
holidays.origin: It marks the adoption of the Rome Statute on July 17, 1998. It is also known as International Criminal Justice Day, and it has been observed since the statute was adopted.
holidays.funFact: The Rome Statute came into force in 2002 after 60 countries had ratified it, and the court sits in The Hague in the Netherlands.

holidays.name: Tell a Joke Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to groan-worthy puns, dad jokes, and knock-knock classics. Everyone is encouraged to spread laughter by telling at least one joke to a friend, coworker, or stranger.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial humor observance popular in holiday calendars, designed to encourage laughter and lighten up the middle of summer.
holidays.funFact: Laughter reduces stress hormones, so telling a bad joke may actually be good for your health, even if the groans are loud.
